chapter: Starting out and leading a band
title: First jobs with Shabbs, Lamb and George Parker
summary: Joseph recalls fixing a horn, a gruelling first parade job with Lamb, then playing with George Parker and a union dance.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah, I had my case right there with your good night. I'd take that one out and play nothing. You couldn't take it out? No. He'd take the time and he'd make you sit down there and he'd ask you questions. And now he'd ask you how many notes in music and how you divide the music. What are seven notes in music? In other words, four notes. You understand? You can make more than that. He'd ask you all them questions like that. Well, sometimes you wouldn't have your mind. He kept you on a snap journey to catch you sometimes. You understand what I mean? Yeah. Well, he'd know why he'd catch you. He'd know you ain't been doing stuff in your horn. Yeah. And after you get there, you get there, you go home, man, get home, clap, blow, blow, blow. He'd know a little old scale out for the mirror of my guard today. You know, the voice piece of music you play with. You go home, bam, Man, you learn that? Man, it's always the highest thing in the world after you learn that through the beastly. So, come back to you say, well, I'm going to try. You see, can you play this? You think you're going to play something? You make all the boys get their horn. About six of us. Get your horn. Guess what he'd put on you? On the sink, go marching in. Don't, don't, don't, don't. Clannets, trumpets. He'd have all that cleats. Clannets, trumpets, bass drum, violin. All students. All students. All students, right there in the house. All bunch of youngsters. Can you remember who else was studying with you at that time? Gilbert Young was, Gilbert was going there too. You know Gilbert Young? Yeah. Wake up at the, at the post office. Gilbert, well Gilbert used to be the worst one in the bunch. Oh, man, I troubled Gilbert. See his son Gilbert to take, you know what he'd do, Bill? Gilbert would spend his money. That time Gilbert was living none, yeah. Gilbert used to be, you know, like all kids. Yeah. Gilbert would go to the show. I ain't lie, I was going to the show too. I went to the show too. Take the horn, go in the show, come back, you all, they went to the lesson. At the same time I'd be lying, I was lying. I ain't even say I didn't lie, I didn't lie too. We used to do that. So, we got into him, said let's make up my mind. This man, we might have to go ahead. Well, he was the only one lying you could pay two bits of lesson. See, that other fella was charging a dollar and something. That time they had a fella in the other time they called a fair boss. He was charging a dollar and something to go get lessons. And they had a Monetta across the river, you know Fess. Well, Fess was charging kind of high, because Fess had a lot of them white boys across the river. Well, we couldn't fool Fess, that was too much. And I'll tell you another story I took and done. Now I learned how to get my horn really good. I got around them old mans. So, I say to myself, I'm going to do something with this horn right now. I get all them old time musicians. I even got with Shabbs. You know Shabbs was a good trumpet player. Yeah, I heard it. Right behind Lewis. So, one Sunday shot, called me up and said, I got a prayer. I'll never forget a jolly boy prayer. Think he can make it? He said, yeah, I can make it. Man, I knew if I could make it. I went just the same. I went with Shabbs. Man, I done one of them. So, after, come in and get there. Man, I might have, boy, you making a whole lot of noise. That time I had that little short trumpet like that. Burn that, burn that, son. Yeah. And while I was doing trinchement work, I find horn and I passed the horn up myself. I passed the horn up. Sheep would tell you the same thing. Sheep had an old horn too. I'll tell you about this. Same time, when that thing's on story, that, sheep had old horn, it was patched. It was all bent up. Well, I took the horn apart. I was doing metal work. I could do it good. I fixed the horn up. He had learned the horn to kick Howard. What Howard took and done. Howard took and, see, after I fixed the horn for sheep, Howard took the horn. Sheep come out his horn from Howard. Howard had a job to go play at night. She'd tell you about that. So, him and Howard had it. So, I said, sheep, Howard, I learned you my horn. I learned you my horn. What Howard was good to, you understand? Well, Howard had done good to watch me too. Howard was hiring me too. So, the only one that asked him, thing back. I turned around there. I goes on a, this is my cousin. I goes with, with a lamb. You remember lamb? You spread the old record? He gets the old, the old, the old noise. You know the old noise uptown. I think. So, I called him. But, they like, corn. Lamb said, you want to make, you want to make a couple of hours? Yeah, I'm making. Man, I started with lamb. Round about 11.30. Man, my lift got so weak. And I thought to come on home. I told lamb, I can't make it no more. I said, don't be scared, boy. Don't be scared. So, man, I took him. You know, drink maybe by drinking. And maybe, you want me to come up and bat him. So, I said, 12 o'clock. We was up around, uh, Louisiana. You know where they make the tongue come down, St. Charles. I said, sheep, they ain't no use me going to myself. I said, they ain't no use me going back home. I ain't got to St. Charles. And St. Charles and Louisiana. I said, I said, I'm going to put it in the good Lord's hand. I'm going to try to make it. And, man, do you know I made it? I made it. I come all the way down to Canal Street. That time, we had to go to Canal Street and come back up and walk it. Long way. Long way. Well, we made a stop on Magazine. Somewhere around St. George Street, there's the feeders up there, you know. They give us something neat. So, lamb said, you know how you feel better now, boy? I said, yeah, man, I felt good. When they hit the Poirier Avenue, going out towards South Street, you understand? I felt more better, you understand what I mean? When they hit the way up around Nashville. Man, I can make another one like that again tomorrow. Make another one like that. That's how I begin to make myself. You understand what I'm doing? So, after another boy, I started playing with George E. Parker at the Happy Landing. Tell you. See me, I had plenty of knowledge. So, at night, the Union had was 12 fans at the Jitsa T-Room. Jitsa T-Room. With George E. Parker, I played with George E. Parker. I had me, George E. Parker, Michael Lee. Uh, his boy played guitar. I know you didn't hear about him. He drives a lumber truck. The lumber truck. The lumber truck.

back in town, Ruben, Ruben they called him. Ruben, Ruben can tell you. Well we had about nine pieces and Dave, well Dave Band was up there too playing. And so Dave, uh, Dave was telling me. So I'm gonna tell you man, I got up there, Mike I swear to Jesus Christ boy, there was there and Bigfoot Billy was with it. Stay down there, I'm trying to never man you sure be asking me that. So Mike, Mike seen Dave with Dave Band, Dave played a couple of them. Man he said no lie Mike, I'm not lying. Mike in California, Mike packed up his home and said man I ain't trying to get that band. I said what's the matter? I said you're getting paid like it but. Man I know where I got the strength at. In the same building I got up and I got against Dave. Me and Dave had it. So people come up there, so Mike, a little museum come out and I said, I didn't know you could do that. I said many things I can do, I can't do, I tried myself in doing it, playing music, you understand what I mean? So that got all right. Well after we finished, the youths had come all, all band had to play about three hours to play. And the way the union was funded the music to build money for the union, you understand what I mean? But the union wasn't like it is, nah. The union didn't have the money like they got not, you understand me? So we turned around there, we turned around, I get the job at the Masonic Temple on St. Charles on the 14th floor up there.
